primitives.name: Promissory Language Regex Filter
primitives.verbatim_quote: Banned promotional language (existing v1 — kept for completeness) | ID | Pattern | Action | Notes | |---|---|---|---| | BS-001 | `\b(guaranteed\|lock\|sure thing\|easy money\|free money\|can't lose)\b` | block | Tout language.
primitives.assumptions: Assumes natural language text is tokenized and case-normalized before regex application.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Regex fails when embedded within larger documents (e.g., HTML attributes) or when clever synonyms evade the pattern.

primitives.name: Factor Activation State Invariant
primitives.verbatim_quote: | ID | Rule | Action | |---|---|---| | BS-010 | A factor with `activationState !== 'activated'` MUST NOT contribute to any `confidence`, `edge`, or `trueEV` field exposed in a public API response.
primitives.assumptions: Assumes a well-defined enum of activation states {'unregistered', 'shadow', 'activated'} and a clear separation between internal and public data models.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Violates when shadow factors leak into public responses due to serialization bugs or missing middleware assertions.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic to the resource capability model in programming language theory, where 'activated' is a capability that must be present to access certain memory regions.
layer2.telemetry: Count of leaked shadow fields per deployment, mean time between violations.
